opportunity: Chronic wounds need dressings that adhere conformally, retain moisture, absorb exudate and self-heal; a cell-friendly enzymatic crosslinker forms in-situ adherent gels under mild conditions.
tg_fit: mTG-crosslinked gelatin (and gelatin/alginate) hydrogels are actively studied as self-healing, drug-loaded wound dressings; already demonstrated in vitro/in vivo, not yet a marketed TG dressing.
evidence: Enzymatically-crosslinked gelatin hydrogels with self-healing behaviour and antibiotic loading are reported as promising wound dressings with in vitro/in vivo biocompatibility.

sources.title: Enzymatically-Crosslinked Gelatin Hydrogels with Nanostructured Architecture and Self-Healing Performance for Potential Use as Wound Dressings
Characterization of an Enzyme-Catalyzed Crosslinkable Hydrogel as a Wound Dressing in Skin Tissue Engineering

verification.note: Multiple peer-reviewed studies of TG/enzyme-crosslinked gelatin wound dressings; preclinical stage.

opportunity: Corneal perforations and lacerations need transparent, sutureless sealing that avoids astigmatism and supports epithelial regeneration; adhesives must tolerate high intraocular burst pressures.
tg_fit: Gelatin-based ocular adhesives (GelCORE) and gelatin-mTG have been proposed/tested as sutureless corneal sealants; early clinical study of a sutureless ophthalmic hydrogel is registered. mTG is one crosslinking route among photocrosslinking.
evidence: Gelatin-based bioadhesive hydrogels seal corneal injuries sutureless in preclinical models tolerating high burst pressures, and a sutureless ophthalmic hydrogel is in an early clinical study.

sources.title: Sutureless repair of corneal injuries using naturally derived bioadhesive hydrogels
Corneal Sealants in Pre-Clinical Development (review)
A Single-Center Clinical Study of Sutureless Ophthalmic Hydrogel for Corneal Wound Repair (NCT07638215)

verification.note: Multiple sources; gelatin adhesives advancing to clinic, though leading products photocrosslink rather than use mTG.

sector: Ophthalmology - retinal tear / detachment tamponade patch
opportunity: Retinal breaks need an atraumatic biocompatible patch that covers the tear and supports reattachment without damaging the neural retina.
tg_fit: Gelatin-mTG complex has been directly tested in vivo: injected into the vitreous, it covered retinal tears >7 days and achieved reattachment in rabbit models without structural retinal damage.
evidence: In rabbit vitrectomy models, gelatin-mTG covered the retinal tear for more than 7 days with reattachment in all treated eyes and low inflammation.

sources.title: Feasibility of using gelatin-microbial transglutaminase complex to repair experimental retinal detachment in rabbit eyes
Gelatin-based biomimetic tissue adhesive: potential for retinal reattachment

verification.note: Directly uses gelatin-mTG in vivo; two peer-reviewed sources. Remains preclinical.

opportunity: Buccal and transmucosal delivery needs films/gels that adhere to wet mucosa and resist dissolution to prolong residence and control release.
tg_fit: TG-crosslinked gelatin (and gelatin/alginate) forms rigid, slow-degrading, drug-loaded matrices; demonstrated for drug-release coatings, but buccal-specific TG use is largely extrapolated/research-stage rather than proven.
evidence: TGase crosslinks gelatin/alginate hydrogels to >90% with tunable rigidity and antibiotic slow-release, supporting durable mucoadhesive drug-delivery matrices.

sources.title: Transglutaminase Cross-Linked Gelatin-Alginate-Antibacterial Hydrogel as Drug Delivery-Coatings
Mucoadhesive Enhancement of Gelatine by Crosslinking for Buccal Application

verification.note: TG crosslinking of gelatin for drug delivery is proven; direct buccal-mucosa TG application is inferential.

opportunity: Pulmonary air leak is the most common complication of lung surgery (up to 60% morbidity); sealants must bond wet, moving, compliant lung tissue and withstand cyclic pressure.
tg_fit: TG is used as a crosslinker in lung-mimetic gelatin/tannic-acid sealants that seal air leaks in rat/swine models; the marketed comparator (Progel) is PEG/albumin, not TG, so mTG here remains preclinical.
evidence: A lung-mimetic hydrofoam sealant incorporating transglutaminase-type crosslinking rapidly sealed air leak and restored lung mechanics in rat and swine models.

sources.title: Lung-Mimetic Hydrofoam Sealant to Treat Pulmonary Air Leak
Progel Pleural Air Leak Sealant (BD) - marketed comparator

verification.note: TG appears as a crosslinker in preclinical lung sealants; marketed products in this space are non-TG.

opportunity: Nerve repair benefits from atraumatic bonding that preserves fascicular alignment, reduces scarring/fibrosis and shortens operative time versus microsutures.
tg_fit: The established clinical glue is fibrin (FXIIIa-crosslinked); a gelatin-mTG glue with stronger, blood-free adhesion is a logical but largely hypothetical extension not yet validated for nerve coaptation.
evidence: Fibrin glue (FXIIIa crosslinking) is clinically used for nerve coaptation with outcomes comparable to sutures; a systematic review/meta-analysis supports feasibility.

sources.title: A systematic review and meta-analysis on the use of fibrin glue in peripheral nerve repair
Fibrin glue as a stabilization strategy in peripheral nerve repair with porous conduits

verification.note: Sector value proven with fibrin/FXIIIa; mTG-specific nerve use is hypothetical.

opportunity: Glue fixation of mesh reduces chronic post-op pain versus tacks/staples while providing adequate attachment strength in laparoscopic hernia repair.
tg_fit: Clinically used adhesives are fibrin (FXIIIa) and cyanoacrylate; a gelatin-mTG adhesive could provide cell-friendly, blood-free fixation but is hypothetical/untested for mesh fixation.
evidence: Meta-analysis and literature reviews show tissue glue mesh fixation reduces chronic pain with comparable recurrence versus tacks; adhesives used are fibrin and cyanoacrylate.

sources.title: Tissue Adhesives for Hernia Mesh Fixation: A Literature Review
Mesh fixation at laparoscopic inguinal hernia repair: meta-analysis comparing tissue glue and tack fixation

verification.note: Sector proven for fibrin/cyanoacrylate; mTG application is hypothetical.

opportunity: Anastomotic leak (4-21%) is a dreaded complication; a sealant that reinforces the suture/staple line and seals against luminal pressure would reduce morbidity.
tg_fit: A biomimetic sealant of gelatin + mTG (mimicking clot formation with non-blood proteins) achieved hemostasis and high adhesive/cohesive strength in vivo, positioning it for anastomotic reinforcement; preclinical.
evidence: Gelatin-mTG biomimetic sealant reached ~320 mmHg burst pressure and complete hemostasis in ~2.5 min in a rat liver model, proposed for anastomosis/vascular fortification.

sources.title: Biomimetic sealant based on gelatin and microbial transglutaminase: an initial in vivo investigation
Clinical results after external reinforcement of colorectal anastomosis: a systematic review

verification.note: Gelatin-mTG sealant demonstrated in vivo; direct GI-anastomosis leak-prevention data still limited.

opportunity: Stable collagen coatings and crosslinked gingival/periodontal tissue improve implant osseointegration, cell adhesion and reduce inflammation; oral tissues are wet and enzyme-rich.
tg_fit: TG crosslinks collagen on titanium implants (hydrolytically/proteolytically stable, pro-osteogenic) and stiffens gingival tissue reducing inflammatory cytokines; preclinical/ex vivo.
evidence: TG-crosslinked collagen on titanium resists degradation and promotes osteogenic differentiation of MSCs; ex vivo gingival crosslinking increased stiffness and reduced inflammatory cytokines.

sources.title: Transglutaminase enables hydrolytically/proteolytically stable crosslinking of collagen on titanium and promotes osteogenic differentiation

verification.note: Single strong peer-reviewed source plus related oral-mucosa TG substrate biology; preclinical.

opportunity: Delivering cells or engineered tissue to organs (e.g. infarcted myocardium) needs a cytocompatible scaffold that both retains cells and adheres to host tissue.
tg_fit: mTG-crosslinked gelatin scaffolds incorporating cell-adhesion proteins (fibronectin/vitronectin) enhance cell proliferation and are used as cell-delivery matrices; established research tool.
evidence: TGase-mediated gelatin matrices incorporating cell-adhesion factors significantly enhanced cell proliferation and serve as tissue-engineering scaffolds and cell-delivery patches.

sources.title: Transglutaminase-mediated gelatin matrices incorporating cell adhesion factors as a biomaterial for tissue engineering
Transglutaminase crosslinked gelatin as a tissue engineering scaffold

verification.note: Well-established mTG-gelatin scaffold research; two peer-reviewed sources.

opportunity: Bioadhesives that close full-thickness skin incisions with precise edge alignment can outperform sutures on healing, scarring and speed.
tg_fit: TG-catalyzed conjugation between hydrogel glutamine and tissue amine groups is a core adhesion mechanism; recent (2025) TG-reinforced HA and TG-containing hydrogels close skin incisions in rodents, beating fibrin/cyanoacrylate in some models.
evidence: A 2025 TG-reinforced hyaluronic-acid bioadhesive enabled immediate suture-free skin closure with better edge alignment and scar-reduced healing than sutures in mice.

sources.title: Transglutaminase-Reinforced Hyaluronic Acid Bioadhesive for Suture-Free Wound Closure and Scar-Reduced Healing (2025)
Injectable self-healing hydrogel adhesives with firm tissue adhesion for sutureless wound closure

verification.note: TG-driven tissue adhesion for skin closure shown in recent peer-reviewed in vivo studies.

opportunity: Post-op adhesions cause pain, obstruction and infertility; a barrier must be applicable, biocompatible, stay in place, then degrade after healing.
tg_fit: TG-catalyzed crosslinked polysaccharide/collagen and gelatin membranes are studied as biodegradable anti-adhesion barriers; TG provides in-situ, blood-free crosslinking, but data are limited/preclinical.
evidence: Gelatin-based and TG-catalyzed crosslinked composite membranes reduce postoperative peritoneal adhesions in rodent cecum models via barrier and anti-inflammatory effects.

sources.title: Single-Step Engineered Gelatin-Based Hydrogel for Prevention of Postoperative Adhesion and Promotion of Wound Healing
Barrier materials for prevention of surgical adhesions: systematic review

verification.note: Gelatin/crosslinked-membrane anti-adhesion is preclinical; TG-specific role is one of several crosslinkers.

opportunity: Cartilage implants notoriously fail to integrate with host tissue; a bioadhesive that bonds the graft to surrounding cartilage improves fixation and repair.
tg_fit: mTG significantly improves adhesion of GelMA implants to human cartilage (5.82 vs 2.87 kPa) and is compatible with photocrosslinking for a dual-crosslinked, cell-laden, host-bonding hydrogel; preclinical/ex vivo + rabbit.
evidence: Adding mTG roughly doubled ex vivo adhesive strength of GelMA to human cartilage and enabled a dual-crosslinked cell-laden hydrogel bonding to host cartilage.

sources.title: Microbial Transglutaminase Improves ex vivo Adhesion of Gelatin Methacryloyl Hydrogels to Human Cartilage
Enzyme-Cross-linked Gelatin Hydrogel with Cartilage ECM and ADSCs for Hyaline Cartilage Regeneration in Rabbits

verification.note: Direct quantitative mTG cartilage adhesion data plus in vivo enzyme-crosslinked gelatin cartilage repair.

sector: Endoscopic submucosal dissection - submucosal cushion & defect/stenosis prevention
opportunity: After esophageal/GI ESD, mucosal defects cause post-op stenosis and dysphagia; an endoscopically deliverable material that adheres to and covers the submucosal defect reduces stenosis.
tg_fit: An alginate/gelatin/TG/Ca2+ powder delivered through the endoscope forms a hydrogel in situ, is crosslinked by TG, adheres to the submucosal layer >2 weeks, and reduced esophageal stenosis in rats.
evidence: In-situ crosslinkable alginate/gelatin/TG powder adhered to the submucosal layer for over two weeks and reduced esophageal stenosis severity in a rat submucosal-exfoliation model.

sources.title: Prevention of esophageal stenosis via in situ cross-linkable alginate/gelatin powder in a submucosal exfoliation model in rats
A novel gel provides durable submucosal cushion for EMR and ESD

verification.note: TG-crosslinked gelatin/alginate directly used for ESD stenosis prevention in vivo; two peer-reviewed sources.

opportunity: Watertight dural closure is imperative after cranial/spinal surgery; inadequate sealing causes CSF leak with serious sequelae, and sutured dura alone often leaks.
tg_fit: Gelatin-transglutaminase sealant compositions (patented) crosslink gelatin to seal CSF/fluid leaks as a suture adjunct; related gelatin glues give watertight dural closure to 28 days in rat durotomy. Non-TG PEG sealants (DuraSeal) are the marketed incumbents.
evidence: Gelatin-transglutaminase sealant patents claim gelatin crosslinking sufficient to seal CSF, and a gelatin glue provided effective watertight dural closure at 1/7/28 days in a rat durotomy model.

sources.title: Usefulness of a New Gelatin Glue Sealant System for Dural Closure in a Rat Durotomy Model
Gelatin-transglutaminase hemostatic dressings and sealants (patent US9655988)

verification.note: Gelatin sealant dural data strong; TG-specific dural sealing mainly from patents, not clinical trials.

sector: Vascular anastomosis sealant / sutureless vessel bonding
opportunity: Vascular suture lines leak and sutureless anastomosis needs an elastic sealant with strong adhesion that withstands arterial pressure.
tg_fit: Gelatin-mTG sealants achieve fibrin-comparable modulus and are proposed for vascular anastomosis/graft fortification; gelatin-elastin-like-polypeptide elastic sealants reach ~34 kPa burst in porcine anastomosis. Preclinical.
evidence: mTG-crosslinked gelatin sealants match fibrin-sealant modulus and are proposed for arterial/vein hemostasis and anastomosis fortification; elastic gelatin-ELP sealants withstand ~34 kPa in ex vivo porcine anastomosis.

sources.title: Biomimetic sealant based on gelatin and microbial transglutaminase (vascular fortification)
Engineering elastic sealants based on gelatin and elastin-like polypeptides for endovascular anastomosis

verification.note: Gelatin-mTG proposed for vascular use; direct anastomosis validation still emerging.

opportunity: Bone and dental-pulp regeneration need stable, stiff, cytocompatible scaffolds that support osteogenic differentiation and remain in the defect.
tg_fit: mTG-crosslinked gelatin (with hyaluronan/chondroitin) forms stable stiff hydrogels that upregulate osteogenic markers in dental pulp stem cells; established regenerative-biomaterials research.
evidence: mTG-crosslinked gelatin/GAG semi-IPN hydrogels showed improved stiffness/stability and enhanced osteogenic differentiation (osteocalcin/osteopontin) of dental pulp stem cells.

sources.title: Gelatin-GAG semi-IPN hydrogels via microbial-transglutaminase crosslinking enhance osteogenic potential of dental pulp stem cells
Transglutaminase crosslinked gelatin as a tissue engineering scaffold

verification.note: Two peer-reviewed sources; mTG-gelatin bone/pulp scaffolds well documented; research stage.

sector: Ocular / mucosal in-situ gelling drug delivery
opportunity: Eye-drops clear rapidly; mucoadhesive in-situ gels prolong precorneal residence and bioavailability, reducing dosing frequency.
tg_fit: TG-crosslinked gelatin can build durable slow-release mucoadhesive matrices, but ocular in-situ gels are dominated by ion/temperature-responsive polymers; TG use here is conceptual/hypothetical.
evidence: In-situ gelling mucoadhesive systems markedly extend ocular residence; TG-crosslinked gelatin provides durable drug-release matrices but is not established for ophthalmic in-situ gels.

sources.title: Research progress of in-situ gelling ophthalmic drug delivery systems
Transglutaminase Cross-Linked Gelatin-Alginate Hydrogel for drug delivery

verification.note: No direct evidence of TG in ocular in-situ gels; opportunity is inferential.

sector: ENT - tympanic membrane perforation repair adjunct
opportunity: Myringoplasty graft uptake depends on holding grafts (fascia/cartilage) against the eardrum; a biocompatible adhesive/scaffold could stabilize grafts and support regeneration, and biologic adjuncts (e.g. PRP) already show benefit.
tg_fit: No reported use of TG/mTG in tympanic membrane repair; a cytocompatible gelatin-mTG patch is a plausible but currently hypothetical adjunct/scaffold.
evidence: Biologic adjuncts such as PRP improve tympanic-membrane perforation repair, indicating room for regenerative adhesives, but no TG-specific evidence was found.

sources.title: The Efficacy of Platelet-Rich Plasma in the Repair of Tympanic Membrane Perforation

verification.note: No TG evidence in this sector; included as diverse hypothetical opportunity.
